title: Major city health hub closure extended as asbestos tests continue
text:

A community health centre in Canberra city will be shut for longer as specialist investigations continue after asbestos-containing material was found in a plant room.

The City Health Centre was set to be closed for at least three days but will now remain shut until at least Friday, July 10, while the government acts on the advice of specialist consultants.

The Canberra Times on Wednesday revealed the building had been closed after a positive test result for asbestos was returned on Monday, following routine maintenance.

Infrastructure Canberra said it would provide a further update as soon as the next steps for the building, located at the corner of Moore Street and Alinga Street, were confirmed.

"The health and safety of occupants remains our highest priority and decisions regarding reoccupation of the building will continue to be guided by expert advice," the agency said in a statement on Thursday.

"Services that usually operate from 1 Moore Street are closed or temporarily working from other locations. Please contact the relevant service provider for information on their service accessibility during this period.

"Arrangements are being put in place to support affected tenants and their operational decisions in minimising disruption to services wherever possible."

On Wednesday, the government said specialist consultants had recommended the building be closed on Tuesday, and it would remain shut on Wednesday and Thursday.

The building is also home to the MSI Canberra Abortion and Contraception Clinic, BreastScreen ACT, the canTEST pill testing service and the Canberra Innovation Network (CBRIN). The ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal was also formerly located in the building.

Construction of the building, originally for the ACT Health Service, began in the 1970s before self-government, when asbestos was still widely used in building products in Australia.

Australia started introducing asbestos bans in the mid-1980s and totally banned the manufacture, use, reuse, import and sale of all asbestos forms in 2003.

Asbestos is a risk to health if the fibres become airborne and are inhaled, which can lead to mesothelioma, a normally rare cancer, a fact sheet issued in 2021 by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation said.

"People who were exposed to asbestos in the workplace - such as in its mining, manufacture or installation - are at greater risk than people who occupy buildings constructed with asbestos products," the CSIRO fact sheet said.

The government identified the Moore Street building for sale as part of a Commonwealth asset recycling program more than a decade ago.

The 2016-17 ACT budget funded a business case for relocating the City Health Centre after its planned sale in the asset recycling scheme, which offered states and territories bonuses from the Commonwealth if they sold ageing infrastructure and reinvested the proceeds in agreed projects.

But the ACT government has retained the building and provided $3.1 million in funding between 2022 and 2024 to renovate office space and expand the Canberra Innovation Network's footprint.

"Future expansion of CBRIN at 1 Moore Street is supported subject to future demand for floor space, viable relocation options for existing tenants and provision of refurbishment funding through normal budget processes," Chief Minister Andrew Barr told the Legislative Assembly's standing committee on economics, industry and recreation in February 2025.

The ACT government shut or partially closed several public schools after asbestos-contaminated play sand was identified in late 2025.

"The laws in the ACT around asbestos removal are some of the most rigorous in the country. While we understand the risk of exposure to the traces of asbestos in these products was identified as low, under ACT work health and safety laws, any products containing asbestos must be assessed and removed by licensed asbestos assessors," Education Minister Yvette Berry told the Legislative Assembly in December 2025.
